title: Symmetry-permuting entanglers for non-invertible symmetry-protected topological phases
abstract: 1+1D symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases with invertible symmetry can be characterized by the symmetric entanglers: globally symmetric finite-depth local unitary circuits that generate representative ground states from a product state. For non-invertible symmetries, however, distinct SPT phases, such as the three $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ SPT phases, may not be connected by any symmetric entangler. We show that the three $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ SPT phases can nevertheless be connected by \emph{symmetry-permuting} finite-depth local unitary circuits, realizing dualities predicted by topological quantum field theory (TQFT). We construct an explicit matrix product unitary connecting two of the $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ SPT phases, and show that its action on string order parameters reproduces the anyon permutation predicted by the TQFT duality.
summary: This work tackles the challenge of connecting distinct non-invertible SPT phases using quantum circuits. The authors develop and construct 'symmetry-permuting entanglers' realized as Matrix Product Unitaries. These circuits successfully demonstrate the realization of TQFT dualities by inducing specific anyon permutations on the system's order parameters.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to characterize and connect different Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) phases, particularly when the underlying symmetry is non-invertible.
main_result: The authors construct explicit symmetry-permuting entanglers, realized as Matrix Product Unitary circuits, that successfully connect distinct $	ext{Rep}(D_8)$ SPT phases, realizing dualities predicted by TQFT.
method: The methodology involves deriving the required unitary circuits by solving local symmetry-pulling-through constraints, leading to the construction of a symmetry-permuting entangler.
model_or_system: The focus is on 1+1D SPT phases characterized by a fusion category $C$, specifically examining the $	ext{Rep}(D_8)$ symmetry group. The physics is analyzed using the framework of Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT).
key_observables: String order parameters, anyon permutations (generating the $S_3$ group), and the action of the entangler on these parameters.
important_parameters: The bond dimension of the Matrix Product Unitary (MPU) circuit, and the specific structure of the non-invertible symmetry group $D_8$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a microscopic realization for 'active dualities' via a finite-depth local circuit, and initially assumes the MPU tensor has bond dimension two.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the SymTFT setup on a cylinder ($\Sigma 	imes I$), relating the symmetry boundary ($\Sigma$) to the physical boundary ($I$). Figure 2 diagrammatically shows the local pulling-through equation involving the crossing tensor $X_a$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical need for symmetry-permuting entanglers for non-invertible symmetries. It then develops the mathematical machinery by deriving the constraints on the MPU tensor, constructing the explicit circuit for the $	ext{Rep}(D_8)$ case, and finally verifying the resulting anyon transformations.
why_interesting: The connection between abstract topological field theory dualities (like FAD) and concrete, finite-depth quantum circuit realizations is highly relevant for understanding the computational power and physical constraints of topological quantum memory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. SymTFT setup on Σ × I, where Σ is a 2-manifold and I is the interval. D is the reference Dirichlet boundary condition, and BQ is the physical boundary condition. Vµ is the space of local operators which tells us how the bulk anyons µ can end on the physical boundary. W µ a is the space of junctions between µ and the symmetry line a which lives on the reference boundary. Compactifying the interval leads to a C-symmetric 1+1d system Q, with the anyon µ turning into an a-twisted sector local operator O. [9]

FIG. 2. Diagrammatic form of the local pulling-through equation. Black lines denote physical legs. The symmetry MPO tensor is drawn as a circle with blue virtual legs, the entangler MPO tensor as a square with red virtual legs, and the crossing tensor Xa implements the exchange of the symmetry and entangler virtual spaces.

FIG. 3. Endpoint pulling-through in three stages. Left: the initial local configuration with endpoint tensor Γa above the entangler. Middle: after applying bulk pulling-through, the endpoint is still the original Γa on the top, while the symmetry line has moved to the bottom and the residual crossing tensor Xa explicitly connects the top endpoint leg to the bottom network. Right: Xa is absorbed into a new endpoint tensor eΓφ(a), yielding the transformed endpoint equation.
